```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

if (file.exists("data/processed/hh_all.rds")) {
  hh_all <- readRDS("data/processed/hh_all.rds")
} else {
  src <- list.files("scripts", pattern = "^read_hh\\.R$",
                    ignore.case = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  source(src[1])
}

# safety net: any leftover -9999 (some files write it as -9999.0) becomes NA
hh_all <- hh_all |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ ifelse(.x <= -9998, NA_real_, .x)))
```

## C1. Site overview
```{r}
#| label: site-overview
snap_file <- list.files("data/snapshots", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
snap <- read_csv(snap_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

my_sites <- c("AU-Ctr", "CN-Dan", "CR-Fsc", "DE-Tha", "US-MBP")
my_snap <- snap |>
  filter(site_id %in% my_sites) |>
  arrange(site_id) |>
  mutate(country = case_when(
    substr(site_id, 1, 2) == "AU" ~ "Australia",
    substr(site_id, 1, 2) == "CN" ~ "China",
    substr(site_id, 1, 2) == "CR" ~ "Costa Rica",
    substr(site_id, 1, 2) == "DE" ~ "Germany",
    substr(site_id, 1, 2) == "US" ~ "USA"))

my_snap |>
  transmute(`Site ID` = site_id, Name = site_name, Country = country, IGBP = igbp,
            `Lat (°)` = round(location_lat, 3), `Lon (°)` = round(location_long, 3),
            `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year, Hub = data_hub,
            `Data DOI / ID` = product_id) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: site-map
#| fig-cap: "Locations of my five flux towers."
world <- map_data("world")
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey85", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = my_snap, aes(location_long, location_lat), colour = "red", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = my_snap, aes(location_long, location_lat, label = site_id),
            vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  coord_fixed(1.3, xlim = c(-180, 180), ylim = c(-60, 85)) +
  labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## C2. Data coverage
```{r}
#| label: coverage
#| fig-cap: "Share of half hours with measured NEE (NEE_VUT_REF_QC == 0) per tower and year."
cov <- hh_all |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(share_measured = mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC %in% 0), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(cov, aes(x = year, y = site, fill = share_measured)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                       name = "NEE measured") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1996, 2026, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Tower") +
  theme_minimal()
```
DE-Tha has the best NEE coverage, with 54 to 55% of half-hours measured in its best years (2007, 2009, 2017, 2012 and 2004), and it also has the longest record (1996-2026). Even at its best, though, about 45% of the half-hours are gap-filled, and no tower comes close to full coverage. The DE-Tha tile for 2026 is dark because the year isn’t finished, and the first year (1996) is dark as well, so those years have little measured NEE.
CN-Dan has no measured NEE (or GPP, or RECO), and AU-Cte has NEE but is missing the other measurements

```{r}
#| label: coverage-best
cov |> arrange(desc(share_measured)) |> slice_head(n = 5)
```

## C3. Summary statistics
```{r}
#| label: summary-stats
vars <- c(TA_F = "TA_F (°C)",
          SW_IN_F = "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)",
          VPD_F = "VPD_F (hPa)",
          P_F = "P_F (mm)",
          NEE_VUT_REF = "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          GPP_NT_VUT_REF = "GPP (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          RECO_NT_VUT_REF = "RECO (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          H_F_MDS = "H (W m⁻²)",
          LE_F_MDS = "LE (W m⁻²)")

# mean annual precipitation sum, using only years with >= 90 % of half hours present
p_annual <- hh_all |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(p_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), p_ok = mean(!is.na(P_F)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(p_ok >= 0.9) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(p_annual = mean(p_sum), .groups = "drop")

site_table <- function(s) {
  d <- hh_all |> filter(site == s)
  cols <- lapply(names(vars), function(v) {
    x <- d[[v]]
    pa <- p_annual$p_annual[p_annual$site == s]
    m <- if (v == "P_F") { if (length(pa) == 0) NA_real_ else pa } else mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    c(m,
      suppressWarnings(min(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      suppressWarnings(max(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      100 * mean(is.na(x)))
  })
  out <- do.call(cbind, cols)
  out[!is.finite(out)] <- NA
  colnames(out) <- vars
  rownames(out) <- c("Mean (P_F: annual sum, mm per year)", "Minimum", "Maximum", "% missing")
  out
}
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-tables
#| results: asis
for (s in sort(unique(hh_all$site))) {
  cat("\n\n**", s, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(site_table(s), digits = 1))
}
```

## C4. Time series
```{r}
#| label: daily
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP and RECO per tower (half-hourly values averaged per day, local standard time). Negative NEE means net uptake of carbon."
#| fig-height: 9
library(tidyr)

# daily mean (needs >= 80 % of the 48 half hours), converted to g C m-2 d-1
daily <- hh_all |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  group_by(site, date) |>
  summarise(across(c(NEE_VUT_REF, GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO_NT_VUT_REF),
                   ~ if (mean(!is.na(.x)) >= 0.8) mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.0378 else NA_real_),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  rename(NEE = NEE_VUT_REF, GPP = GPP_NT_VUT_REF, RECO = RECO_NT_VUT_REF)

daily |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), names_to = "flux", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = flux)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Date", y = expression("Flux (g C m"^-2*" d"^-1*")"), colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
For AU-Cte we only have NEE, and everything else is NA, so we only have the NEE line. There are some noticable gaps in 2014 and 2018
For CN-Dan the data is entirela NA, therefore the table could not be rendered
```{r}
#| label: dd-check
# check my daily NEE against the FLUXMET_DD file of one site (CR-Fsc)
zip_cr  <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "CR-Fsc.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
dd_name <- grep("FLUXMET_DD", unzip(zip_cr, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)
unzip(zip_cr, files = dd_name, exdir = "data/raw/unzipped")

dd <- read_csv(file.path("data/raw/unzipped", dd_name), na = "-9999",
               col_select = any_of(c("TIMESTAMP", "NEE_VUT_REF")),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP = "c", .default = "d")) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(TIMESTAMP, "%Y%m%d"))

chk <- daily |> filter(site == "CR-Fsc") |> select(date, mine = NEE) |>
  inner_join(dd, by = "date")

c(correlation = cor(chk$mine, chk$NEE_VUT_REF, use = "complete.obs"),
  mean_difference = mean(chk$mine - chk$NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## C5.
Diurnal cyclesSeasons are meteorological (Dec–Feb, Mar–May, Jun–Aug, Sep–Nov). For towers south of the equator (AU-Ctr, latitude < 0) the months are shifted by six months, so that "Summer" always means the warm season of that hemisphere. In the tropics (AU-Ctr, CR-Fsc) the seasons are weak and wet and dry seasons would be more meaningful. Hours are local standard time.

```{r}
#| label: diurnal
#| fig-cap: "Mean diurnal cycle of NEE and LE per season and tower (local standard time)."
#| fig-height: 7
library(tidyr)

# only the sign of the latitude matters here (hemisphere)
lat <- c("AU-Ctr" = -16.1, "CN-Dan" = 30.5, "CR-Fsc" = 10.8,
         "DE-Tha" = 51.0, "US-MBP" = 47.5)

season_of <- function(month, lat) {
  m <- ifelse(lat < 0, (month + 5) %% 12 + 1, month)
  case_when(m %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
            m %in% 3:5         ~ "Spring",
            m %in% 6:8         ~ "Summer",
            TRUE               ~ "Autumn")
}

diur <- hh_all |>
  mutate(month  = as.integer(format(time, "%m")),
         hour   = as.integer(format(time, "%H")) + as.integer(format(time, "%M")) / 60,
         season = factor(season_of(month, unname(lat[site])),
                         levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn"))) |>
  group_by(site, season, hour) |>
  summarise(NEE = mean(NEE_VUT_REF, na.rm = TRUE),
            LE  = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, LE), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = c("NEE", "LE"),
                           labels = c("NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)", "LE (W m⁻²)")))

ggplot(diur, aes(hour, value, colour = season)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(variable ~ site, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Hour of day (local standard time)", y = NULL, colour = "Season") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## C6. Your reading
```{r}
#| label: energy-balance
#| fig-cap: "Energy balance closure: H + LE against NETRAD − G, half-hours with measured H and LE only (QC = 0)."
eb <- hh_all |>
  filter(H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |>
  mutate(turb = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS, avail = NETRAD - G_F_MDS) |>
  filter(!is.na(turb), !is.na(avail))

eb_counts <- eb |> count(site, name = "half_hours")
eb_counts

eb_site <- eb_counts |> slice_max(half_hours, n = 1) |> pull(site)
eb1 <- eb |> filter(site == eb_site)

fit <- lm(turb ~ avail, data = eb1)
slope <- unname(coef(fit)[2])

ggplot(eb1, aes(avail, turb)) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 80) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", name = "Half hours") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = paste0(eb_site, ": slope = ", round(slope, 2)),
       x = expression("NETRAD − G (W m"^-2*")"),
       y = expression("H + LE (W m"^-2*")")) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
#| label: comparison
# mean annual NEE sum (g C m-2 yr-1; negative = net uptake), near-complete years only
ann_site <- daily |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))) |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(days = sum(!is.na(NEE)), NEE_sum = sum(NEE, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(days >= 330) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(years_used = n(), NEE_annual_gC = mean(NEE_sum), .groups = "drop")

# seasonal cycle: range of monthly mean GPP (g C m-2 d-1)
season <- daily |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) |>
  group_by(site, month) |>
  summarise(GPP = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(GPP_range = suppressWarnings(max(GPP, na.rm = TRUE) - min(GPP, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(GPP_range = ifelse(is.finite(GPP_range), GPP_range, NA_real_))

# share of NEE that is gap-filled
gapfill <- hh_all |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(pct_gapfilled = 100 * mean(NEE_VUT_REF_QC[!is.na(NEE_VUT_REF_QC)] != 0),
            .groups = "drop")

comparison <- ann_site |>
  full_join(season, by = "site") |>
  full_join(gapfill, by = "site")

knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 1,
             col.names = c("Site", "Years used", "Mean annual NEE (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹)",
                           "Seasonal range of GPP (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)", "% NEE gap-filled"))
```
The five towers are a rainforest in northeast Queensland (AU-Ctr, 16°S), an alpine grassland on the Tibetan Plateau (CN-Dan), a sugar cane field in Costa Rica (CR-Fsc, 10°N, so close to the equator), a spruce forest in Saxony, Germany (DE-Tha) and a peatland in Minnesota, USA (US-MBP). CR-Fsc takes up the most carbon (mean annual NEE −1,045 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹, from only 4 years), followed by DE-Tha (−474, 29 years) and US-MBP (−241, 16 years). Because CR-Fsc is a cropland near the equator, the crop can grow for much of the year, but NEE does not include the carbon removed at harvest, so the carbon the field actually keeps is probably much smaller. DE-Tha has the largest seasonal cycle (monthly mean GPP ranges by 8.4 g C m⁻² d⁻¹, against 4.0 at CR-Fsc and 3.7 at US-MBP), which is consistent with its high latitude 51°N. What surprised me is AU-Ctr: a rainforest with a positive mean annual NEE (+66 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹, a net source) and no usable GPP values. CN-Dan has no NEE, GPP or RECO in the half-hourly file, and at the other four towers 52% (DE-Tha) to 71% (US-MBP) of the NEE half-hours are gap-filled. For the energy balance I used DE-Tha, where the slope of 0.72 means H + LE is only about 72% of the available energy (NETRAD − G), a closure gap that is common for eddy-covariance towers.

## Data and citation
Data come from the FLUXNET Shuttle snapshot `r basename(snap_file)`. Product files (ONEFlux version v1.3, run r1):

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat(paste0("- ", my_snap$fluxnet_product_name), sep = "\n")
```

Variables used: half-hourly `FLUXMET_HH` files with `NEE_VUT_REF` for NEE, `GPP_NT_VUT_REF` and `RECO_NT_VUT_REF` (night-time partitioning) for GPP and RECO, the gap-filled meteorology (`_F`) and `H_F_MDS` / `LE_F_MDS`. A value of −9999 was treated as missing. Time stamps are local standard time.

**Data citations**

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat("\n")
cat(paste0("- ", my_snap$product_citation), sep = "\n")
cat("\n")
```

Pastorello, G. et al. (2020). The FLUXNET2015 dataset and the ONEFlux processing pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Scientific Data* 7, 225. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>

FLUXNET data products were produced and harmonized by eddy covariance regional networks and data processing centers, including AmeriFlux, ChinaFlux, European Fluxes Database, ICOS, JapanFlux, KoFlux, OzFlux, SAEON, and TERN. These products also include a modified version of ERA5 hourly data provided by the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
